title: Why Your Best Students Need Strict Accountability https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2020/02/29/your-best-students-need-strict-accountability/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin challenges the common habit of letting well-behaved, top-performing students slide on minor rule infractions. He argues this favoritism does real harm in three ways: it breeds resentment among peers who notice unequal enforcement, it fosters entitlement in the favored students themselves, and it reinforces a caste-like social hierarchy that mirrors and amplifies existing divisions like looks, money, and popularity. He contends that being treated as special ultimately sets high-performing students up for later struggles with failure, anxiety, or a fragile self-image. His prescription is consistent enforcement for all students regardless of standing, arguing this instills humility and genuine self-worth that will serve them well beyond the classroom.
points: Argues that excusing top students' minor infractions breeds resentment among classmates who notice unequal treatment.
Contends that letting favorites off the hook fosters entitlement and numbs their empathy over time.
Warns that inconsistent enforcement reinforces a social caste system already amplified by looks, money, and popularity.
Claims being treated as 'special' by teachers can set students up for later struggles with failure and anxiety.
Frames consistent accountability for all students as a way to build genuine humility and lasting self-worth.
quotes: Enforcing a consequence based on who the student is—or on the situation, the severity of the misbehavior, or how you happen to be feeling that day—always leads resentment.
As soon as the class notices that you treat some students differently than everyone else, it will obliterate their trust in you.
Believing they’re above the law hardens their heart, numbs their sense of empathy, and sets them up for a big, depressive fall that often doesn’t come until years later.

Being viewed as special eventually becomes an albatross that can lead to the fear of trying and failing. It can even be a catalyst for anxiety, depression, and other mental health issues down the line.
It’s our job, if we’re to do it well, to instill humility, kindness, and true self-worth. To prepare students to stand tall and steady in the face of adversity that will surely come their way.
They carry on inside the heart of every student and rumble into the future.
